claim: Nkx2.2 is one of the earliest and most broadly expressed islet transcription factors.
source: To parse out the spatiotemporal regulation of islet cell differentiation, we used a Neurog3-Cre allele to ablate Nkx2.2, one of the earliest and most broadly expressed islet transcription factors, specifically in the Neurog3+ endocrine progenitor lineage (Nkx2.2△endo).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of Nkx2.2, drawing from established scientific knowledge about this transcription factor.

claim: Many essential components of the β cell transcriptional network that were down-regulated in the Nkx2.2KO mice were maintained in the Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Remarkably, many essential components of the β cell transcriptional network that were down-regulated in the Nkx2.2KO mice, were maintained in the Nkx2.2△endo mice - yet the Nkx2.2△endo mice displayed defective β cell differentiation and recapitulated the Nkx2.2KO phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data comparing gene expression between Nkx2.2KO and Nkx2.2△endo mice, showing differential expression patterns for key transcription factors.

claim: Nkx2.2△endo mice displayed defective β cell differentiation and recapitulated the Nkx2.2KO phenotype.
source: Remarkably, many essential components of the β cell transcriptional network that were down-regulated in the Nkx2.2KO mice, were maintained in the Nkx2.2△endo mice - yet the Nkx2.2△endo mice displayed defective β cell differentiation and recapitulated the Nkx2.2KO phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data showing reduced insulin+ cells and altered endocrine cell populations in Nkx2.2△endo mice similar to Nkx2.2KO mice.

claim: Nkx2.2 is required in the early pancreatic progenitors and has additional essential activities within the endocrine progenitor population.
source: This suggests that Nkx2.2 is not only required in the early pancreatic progenitors, but has additional essential activities within the endocrine progenitor population.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that deletion of Nkx2.2 specifically in the endocrine progenitor lineage recapitulates the global knockout phenotype.

claim: Nkx2.2 functions as an integral component of a modular regulatory program to correctly specify pancreatic islet cell fates.
source: Consistently, we demonstrate Nkx2.2 functions as an integral component of a modular regulatory program to correctly specify pancreatic islet cell fates.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq co-occupancy analysis showing overlap between Nkx2.2, Rfx6, and Neurod1 binding at target genes.

claim: The exocrine pancreas represents the majority of the pancreatic tissue and contains acinar cells that secrete digestive enzymes and ductal cells through which the enzymes are transported into the duodenum.
source: The exocrine pancreas represents the majority of the pancreatic tissue and contains acinar cells that secrete digestive enzymes and the ductal cells through which the enzymes are transported into the duodenum.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about pancreatic anatomy and function.

claim: The endocrine pancreas represents 1–2% of the organ.
source: The endocrine pancreas only represents 1–2% of the organ, but is comprised of hormone-producing islet cells that are critical for the maintenance of glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about pancreatic anatomy.

claim: The endocrine pancreas is comprised of hormone-producing islet cells that are critical for the maintenance of glucose homeostasis.
source: The endocrine pancreas only represents 1–2% of the organ, but is comprised of hormone-producing islet cells that are critical for the maintenance of glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about endocrine pancreas function.

claim: The exocrine and endocrine compartments arise from a common multipotent progenitor population that gradually forms spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor subpopulations during development.
source: Interestingly, although these two compartments have highly disparate functions, they arise from a common multipotent progenitor population that gradually forms spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor subpopulations during development (Burlison et al., 2008; Offield et al., 1996; Pan and Wright, 2011; Zhou et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: A bi-potent duct/endocrine progenitor population is derived from the multipotent progenitor population and subsequently differentiates into a highly restricted endocrine progenitor population that produces all islet cell types.
source: A bi-potent duct/endocrine progenitor population is then derived from the multipotent progenitor population and subsequently differentiates into a highly restricted endocrine progenitor population that produces all islet cell types, including the functionally important insulin-producing β cell lineage.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pancreatic development lineage progression.

claim: The multipotent progenitor population is defined by the expression of Pdx1 and Ptf1a.
source: The multipotent progenitor population is defined by the expression of Pancreatic and duodenal homeobox 1 (Pdx1) and Pancreas transcription factor 1a (Ptf1a), transcriptional regulators that are essential for pancreatic formation; deletion of Pdx1 or Ptf1a leads to pancreatic agenesis (Burlison et al., 2008; Gu et al., 2003; Jonsson et al., 1994; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Offield et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Pdx1 and Ptf1a are essential for pancreatic formation.
source: The multipotent progenitor population is defined by the expression of Pancreatic and duodenal homeobox 1 (Pdx1) and Pancreas transcription factor 1a (Ptf1a), transcriptional regulators that are essential for pancreatic formation; deletion of Pdx1 or Ptf1a leads to pancreatic agenesis (Burlison et al., 2008; Gu et al., 2003; Jonsson et al., 1994; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Offield et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies showing pancreatic agenesis upon deletion.

claim: Deletion of Pdx1 or Ptf1a leads to pancreatic agenesis.
source: The multipotent progenitor population is defined by the expression of Pancreatic and duodenal homeobox 1 (Pdx1) and Pancreas transcription factor 1a (Ptf1a), transcriptional regulators that are essential for pancreatic formation; deletion of Pdx1 or Ptf1a leads to pancreatic agenesis (Burlison et al., 2008; Gu et al., 2003; Jonsson et al., 1994; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Offield et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Neurog3 expression delineates the endocrine progenitor population.
source: A subset of cells from the Pdx1+ Ptf1a+ multipotent progenitors gradually become restricted to the endocrine lineage with the expression of Neurogenin 3 (Neurog3), which delineates the endocrine progenitor population.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pancreatic endocrine development.

claim: Neurog3 is essential for the formation of all six embryonic pancreatic endocrine cell types.
source: Neurog3 is essential for the formation of all six embryonic pancreatic endocrine cell types: the insulin-producing β cells, glucagon-producing α cells, somatostatin-producing δ cells, pancreatic polypeptide-producing PP cells, gastrin-producing G cells, and ghrelin-producing ε cells (Gradwohl et al., 2000; Gu et al., 2002; Heller et al., 2005; Schwitzgebel et al., 2000; Suissa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Mice lacking Neurog3 almost completely fail to form endocrine lineages.
source: Mice lacking Neurog3 almost completely fail to form these endocrine lineages (Gradwohl et al., 2000; Heller et al., 2005; Suissa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: β cells are derived from the Neurog3+ progenitor lineage.
source: Although it is well-established that β cells are derived from the Neurog3+ progenitor lineage, there is still some uncertainty about when and where the β cell lineage is specified during pancreas development.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of pancreatic development.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor cells transition through distinct competence windows in response to Neurog3 induction for each endocrine cell fate, with β cell competence being acquired during a window of development between E10.5 and E16.
source: Interestingly, Johansson et al. (2007) demonstrated that pancreatic progenitor cells transition through distinct competence windows in response to Neurog3 induction for each endocrine cell fate, with β cell competence being acquired during a window of development between embryonic day (E)10.5 and E16 (Johansson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: Nkx2.2, Nkx6.1, Rfx6, Glis3, Insm1 and Neurod1 are essential for β cell specification.
source: Many of the transcription factors that are essential for β cell specification have been identified, including Nkx2.2, Nkx6.1, Rfx6, Glis3, Insm1 and Neurod1; however, we still have an incomplete understanding of how these factors regulate the timing and mechanism of β cell fate induction since they are often expressed both early and throughout pancreas development and are not always restricted to the β cell lineage.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the context of the manuscript.

claim: Nkx2.2, Nkx6.1 and Rfx6 are expressed in multipotent pancreatic progenitors and endocrine progenitors, in addition to their maintained expression in several of the mature endocrine lineages.
source: For example, Nkx2.2, Nkx6.1 and Rfx6 are expressed in multipotent pancreatic progenitors and endocrine progenitors, in addition to their maintained expression in several of the mature endocrine lineages (Arnes et al., 2012b; Jørgensen et al., 2007; Pedersen et al., 2005; Soyer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Glis3 expression is first detected in the bipotent progenitor cells, but is then maintained in the preductal and endocrine progenitors, and ultimately restricted to the β, PP and ductal lineages.
source: Glis3 expression is first detected in the bipotent progenitor cells, but is then maintained in the preductal and endocrine progenitors, and ultimately restricted to the β, PP and ductal lineages (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: Insm1 is expressed in the pancreatic pre-endocrine cells, endocrine progenitor cells and is maintained in all endocrine cell types.
source: Insm1 is similarly expressed in the pancreatic pre-endocrine cells, endocrine progenitor cells and is maintained in all endocrine cell types (Gierl et al., 2006; Mellitzer et al., 2006; Osipovich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Neurod1 can be detected as early as E9.5 in the early glucagon and ghrelin producing cells, but predominantly becomes restricted first to endocrine progenitors and then is maintained in all endocrine lineages.
source: Lastly, Neurod1 can be detected as early as E9.5 in the early glucagon and ghrelin producing cells, but predominantly becomes restricted first to endocrine progenitors and then is maintained in all endocrine lineages (Anderson et al., 2009a; Naya et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Null mutations of Nkx2.2, Nkx6.1, Rfx6, Glis3, Insm1, and Neurod1 cause neonatal lethality likely due to their severe defects in β cell development.
source: Null mutations of all six of these transcriptional regulators cause neonatal lethality likely due to their severe defects in β cell development (Gierl et al., 2006; Naya et al., 1997; Osipovich et al., 2014; Prado et al., 2004; Smith et al., 2010; Sussel et al., 1998); however, it is unknown exactly when each of these factors exerts their functional role in β cell fate specification.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Nkx2.2 is a critical regulator of appropriate islet cell lineage specification during pancreagenesis.
source: Nkx2.2 is a critical regulator of appropriate islet cell lineage specification during pancreagenesis; mice carrying an Nkx2.2 null mutation form reduced numbers of α and β cells and instead form increased numbers of ghrelin-producing ε cells due to defects in cell lineage specification (Prado et al., 2004; Sussel et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: Mice carrying an Nkx2.2 null mutation form reduced numbers of α and β cells and instead form increased numbers of ghrelin-producing ε cells due to defects in cell lineage specification.
source: Nkx2.2 is a critical regulator of appropriate islet cell lineage specification during pancreagenesis; mice carrying an Nkx2.2 null mutation form reduced numbers of α and β cells and instead form increased numbers of ghrelin-producing ε cells due to defects in cell lineage specification (Prado et al., 2004; Sussel et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: β cell fate specification is completely dependent on Nkx2.2 as no β cells are formed in Nkx2.2KO mice.
source: Importantly, β cell fate specification is completely dependent on Nkx2.2 as no β cells are formed in mice carrying a null mutation in Nkx2.2 (Nkx2.2KO) (Sussel et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: Nkx2.2 is co-expressed with Pdx1 throughout the pancreatic progenitor domain, but its expression becomes restricted to the Neurog3+ endocrine progenitor population.
source: Nkx2.2 is co-expressed with Pdx1 throughout the pancreatic progenitor domain, but its expression becomes restricted to the Neurog3+ endocrine progenitor population (Arnes et al., 2012b; Jørgensen et al., 2007; Sussel et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies.

claim: The expression of Neurog3, Nkx6.1, Rfx6 and Neurod1 was significantly reduced in Nkx2.2KO progenitor populations.
source: Nkx2.2 also appears to function at or near the top of the regulatory cascade of transcription factors to specify β cell fate: The expression of Neurog3, Nkx6.1, Rfx6 and Neurod1 was significantly reduced in Nkx2.2KO progenitor populations (Anderson et al., 2009a, 2009b; Chao et al., 2007) (Table 1), suggesting that Nkx2.2 functions within the pancreatic epithelium to influence the derivation of endocrine-committed cells that can enter the appropriate endocrine lineage pathways.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research studies and data in Table 1.

claim: Nkx2.2 mRNA expression was reduced at E15.5 and E18.5 in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Efficient deletion of Nkx2.2 in the Nkx2.2△endo mice was demonstrated by a reduction in Nkx2.2 mRNA expression at E15.5 and E18.5 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Nkx2.2 protein was almost undetectable in the pancreas at E15.5 and P0 in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Consistent with the decrease in Nkx2.2 gene expression, Nkx2.2 protein was almost undetectable in the pancreas at E15.5 and postnatal day (P)0 (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 1B, 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tomato+ cells were found specifically within the endocrine compartment in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Activation of the R26R-Tomato allele was also used to monitor accurate Cre activity within the Nkx2.2△endo mice and, accordingly, Tomato+ (Tom+) cells were found specifically within the endocrine compartment (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data showing Tomato expression in Figures 1B, 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deletion of Nkx2.2 from the endocrine progenitor population did not affect the number of Neurog3-expressing endocrine progenitor cells.
source: Deletion of Nkx2.2 from the endocrine progenitor population did not affect the number of Neurog3-expressing endocrine progenitor cells and Neurog3 expression within the Tomato-labeled, Nkx2.2-deficient cells was maintained (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data in Figures 1D, 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and RNA-Seq data in Table 1.

claim: Neurog3 expression within the Tomato-labeled, Nkx2.2-deficient cells was maintained in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Deletion of Nkx2.2 from the endocrine progenitor population did not affect the number of Neurog3-expressing endocrine progenitor cells and Neurog3 expression within the Tomato-labeled, Nkx2.2-deficient cells was maintained (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data in Figures 1D, 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and RNA-Seq data in Table 1.

claim: Deletion of Nkx2.2 did not affect Sox9 expression.
source: Deletion of Nkx2.2 did not appear to affect the earlier cell populations that give rise to endocrine progenitors since the expression of Sox9, an early progenitor marker that is expressed immediately upstream of Neurog3 in the bipotent progenitor pool from which endocrine cells are derived, was unaffected (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: There were no obvious changes in the exocrine lineage in Nkx2.2△endo mice, as indicated by amylase expression.
source: Consistent with specific deletion of Nkx2.2 from the endocrine progenitor population, there were also no obvious changes in the exocrine lineage, as indicated by amylase expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of pan-endocrine genes ChromograninA, Isl1, and Pax6 was unchanged in the absence of Nkx2.2 at E15.5.
source: Expression of pan-endocrine genes, such as ChromograninA (Chga), Isl1, and Pax6 was also unchanged in the absence of Nkx2.2 at E15.5, and the area and number of Tomato-labeled endocrine lineage cells was also unaffected in the Nkx2.2△endo mice at E15.5 and P0, suggesting endocrine compartment size was not decreased when Nkx2.2 was deleted from the endocrine progenitor cell (Figure 1B,C,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The area and number of Tomato-labeled endocrine lineage cells was unaffected in the Nkx2.2△endo mice at E15.5 and P0.
source: Expression of pan-endocrine genes, such as ChromograninA (Chga), Isl1, and Pax6 was also unchanged in the absence of Nkx2.2 at E15.5, and the area and number of Tomato-labeled endocrine lineage cells was also unaffected in the Nkx2.2△endo mice at E15.5 and P0, suggesting endocrine compartment size was not decreased when Nkx2.2 was deleted from the endocrine progenitor cell (Figure 1B,C,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figures 1B, 1C, 1F, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Endocrine compartment size was not decreased when Nkx2.2 was deleted from the endocrine progenitor cell.
source: Expression of pan-endocrine genes, such as ChromograninA (Chga), Isl1, and Pax6 was also unchanged in the absence of Nkx2.2 at E15.5, and the area and number of Tomato-labeled endocrine lineage cells was also unaffected in the Nkx2.2△endo mice at E15.5 and P0, suggesting endocrine compartment size was not decreased when Nkx2.2 was deleted from the endocrine progenitor cell (Figure 1B,C,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Tomato-labeled endocrine lineage cell area and number were unaffected.

claim: Nkx2.2△endo mice displayed a reduction of insulin+ cells and glucagon+ cells, and increased ghrelin+ cells at E15.5 and P0.
source: Similar to the Nkx2.2KO mice (Prado et al., 2004; Sussel et al., 1998), Nkx2.2△endo mice displayed a reduction of insulin+ (Ins+) cells and glucagon+ (Gcg+) cells, and increased ghrelin+ (Ghrl+) cells at E15.5 and P0 (Figure 2A–H; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figures 2A-H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Gastrin+ cells were decreased at E15.5 in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Gastrin+ (Gast+) cells were decreased at E15.5 (Figure 2I,J), and no changes were observed in somatostatin+ (SST+) cell number at P0 (Figure 2K–L; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figures 2I and 2J.

claim: No changes were observed in somatostatin+ cell number at P0 in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Gastrin+ (Gast+) cells were decreased at E15.5 (Figure 2I,J), and no changes were observed in somatostatin+ (SST+) cell number at P0 (Figure 2K–L; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figures 2K-L and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A small number of insulin+ cells were detected in Nkx2.2△endo mice, unlike the Nkx2.2KO mice which lack all β cells.
source: Unlike the Nkx2.2KO mice which lack all β cells, a small number of Ins+ cells were detected (Figure 2A–L; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which is possibly due to the inability of the Neurog3-Cre allele to completely inactivate Nkx2.2.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 2A-L and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of a small number of insulin+ cells in Nkx2.2△endo mice is possibly due to the inability of the Neurog3-Cre allele to completely inactivate Nkx2.2.
source: Unlike the Nkx2.2KO mice which lack all β cells, a small number of Ins+ cells were detected (Figure 2A–L; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which is possibly due to the inability of the Neurog3-Cre allele to completely inactivate Nkx2.2.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the mechanism underlying the observed phenotype.

claim: Insulin and glucagon expression were significantly decreased in Nkx2.2△endo mice at E15.5 and E18.5.
source: Gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 corresponded to changes in endocrine cell numbers. Insulin (Ins1 and Ins2) and glucagon expression were significantly decreased; there was increased ghrelin expression, and no change in somatostatin gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: Ghrelin expression was increased in Nkx2.2△endo mice at E15.5 and E18.5.
source: Gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 corresponded to changes in endocrine cell numbers. Insulin (Ins1 and Ins2) and glucagon expression were significantly decreased; there was increased ghrelin expression, and no change in somatostatin gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: There was no change in somatostatin gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 corresponded to changes in endocrine cell numbers. Insulin (Ins1 and Ins2) and glucagon expression were significantly decreased; there was increased ghrelin expression, and no change in somatostatin gene expression at E15.5 and E18.5 (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: Gast gene expression was decreased at E15.5 in Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Gast gene expression was also decreased at E15.5, but Gast expression was extinguished from both the wild type and mutant pancreata by E18.5 (Figure 2M), as previously observed (Suissa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: Gast expression was extinguished from both the wild type and mutant pancreata by E18.5.
source: Gast gene expression was also decreased at E15.5, but Gast expression was extinguished from both the wild type and mutant pancreata by E18.5 (Figure 2M), as previously observed (Suissa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M and citation to a previous study.

claim: Nkx2.2△endo mice die shortly after birth between P2 and P4.
source: Similar to the Nkx2.2KO mice, the Nkx2.2△endo mice die shortly after birth between P2 and P4 (Figure 2N).
evidence: This is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2N.

claim: Ppy expression was increased at E15.5 and E18.5 in Nkx2.2△endo embryos.
source: Interestingly, we observed increased pancreatic polypeptide (Ppy) expression at E15.5 and E18.5 in Nkx2.2△endo embryos (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: There was similar upregulation of Ppy in the Nkx2.2KO pancreas compared to the Nkx2.2△endo pancreas, although the magnitude of upregulation was greater in the Nkx2.2△endo embryos.
source: Although this was in contrast to previous studies in which we had observed decreased Ppy gene expression and PP+ cell numbers (Chao et al., 2007; Prado et al., 2004; Sussel et al., 1998), we confirmed that there was similar upregulation of Ppy in the Nkx2.2LacZ/LacZ (Nkx2.2KO) pancreas (Arnes et al., 2012b) compared to the Nkx2.2△endo pancreas, although the magnitude of upregulation was greater in the Nkx2.2△endo embryos (Figure 2M,O).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 2M and 2O.

claim: Upregulation of Ppy RNA correlated with changes in protein in Nkx2.2△endo mice; immunostaining revealed increased PP+ cells at both E15.5 and P0.
source: In Nkx2.2△endo mice, upregulation of Ppy RNA correlated with changes in protein; immunostaining revealed increased PP+ cells at both E15.5 and P0 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: There was no significant difference in Ins+PP+ cells between Nkx2.2△endo mice and controls.
source: While some Ins+PP+ cells could be observed (arrow in Figure 2—figure supplement 2), there was no significant difference between Nkx2.2△endo mice and controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that similar to the ghrelin-expressing cells, whose increased numbers were due to altered ε cell specification at the expense of β cell specification, the excess PP cells did not arise from misexpression of PP in β cells or as a result of β cell reprogramming.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The excess PP cells did not arise from misexpression of PP in β cells or as a result of β cell reprogramming.
source: While some Ins+PP+ cells could be observed (arrow in Figure 2—figure supplement 2), there was no significant difference between Nkx2.2△endo mice and controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that similar to the ghrelin-expressing cells, whose increased numbers were due to altered ε cell specification at the expense of β cell specification, the excess PP cells did not arise from misexpression of PP in β cells or as a result of β cell reprogramming.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ins+PP+ cells were not significantly different between mutant and control.

claim: The novel Ppy phenotype in the Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO mice may result from a change in mouse strain background.
source: We speculate that the novel Ppy phenotype in the Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO mice may result from a change in mouse strain background (see Discussion).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the mechanism underlying the observed phenotype.

claim: There was significant overlap (120 genes) between the differentially expressed genes in Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO mice.
source: Consistent with their similar phenotypes, there was significant overlap (120 genes, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 3A) between the differentially expressed genes (adjusted p-value <0.05), including genes encoding pancreatic hormones (Figure 3B) and important α and β cell regulatory factors, such as Mafa and Mafb (Figure 3C,D; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mafa and Mafb gene expression were decreased in both Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO embryos at E15.5.
source: Consistent with their similar phenotypes, there was significant overlap (120 genes, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 3A) between the differentially expressed genes (adjusted p-value <0.05), including genes encoding pancreatic hormones (Figure 3B) and important α and β cell regulatory factors, such as Mafa and Mafb (Figure 3C,D; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 3C, 3D, and Table 1.

claim: Nkx6.1, Pax4, and Pdx1 were unchanged in Nkx2.2KO embryos at E15.5 and were also not affected in Nkx2.2△endo pancreas at this early time point.
source: Furthermore, several transcription factor genes expressed in endocrine progenitors and involved in β cell specification, such as Nkx6.1, Pax4, and Pdx1, that were unchanged Nkx2.2KO embryos at E15.5 were also not affected in Nkx2.2△endo pancreas at this early time point (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Table 1.

claim: Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 expression were unaffected in the Nkx2.2△endo mice, in sharp contrast to the Nkx2.2KO mice which have reduced expression of these genes.
source: Notably, in sharp contrast to the Nkx2.2KO mice, which have reduced Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 (Anderson et al., 2009a, 2009b; Chao et al., 2007) (Table 1), expression of Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 were unaffected in the Nkx2.2△endo mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3E and Table 1, and citations to previous studies.

claim: Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 gene expression were maintained in E15.5 and E18.5 Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: We performed qRT-PCR analysis to confirm the maintenance of Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 gene expression in E15.5 and E18.5 Nkx2.2△endo mice (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Neurog3 mRNA appeared to be modestly increased at E18.5 in the Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: Although Neurog3 mRNA appeared to be modestly increased at E18.5 in the Nkx2.2△endo mice (Figure 3F), Neurog3+ cells could not be detected by immunostaining in perinatal animals (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Neurog3+ cells could not be detected by immunostaining in perinatal Nkx2.2△endo animals.
source: Although Neurog3 mRNA appeared to be modestly increased at E18.5 in the Nkx2.2△endo mice (Figure 3F), Neurog3+ cells could not be detected by immunostaining in perinatal animals (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 3G and 3H.

claim: Although Nkx2.2 regulates Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 expression within the pancreatic progenitor population, regulation of these genes within the endocrine progenitor cells becomes independent of Nkx2.2.
source: These results suggest that although Nkx2.2 regulates Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 expression within the pancreatic progenitor population, regulation of Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 expression within the endocrine progenitor cells becomes independent of Nkx2.2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that these genes are maintained in Nkx2.2△endo mice but reduced in Nkx2.2KO mice.

claim: Maintenance of Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 expression in the absence of Nkx2.2 is not sufficient for appropriate islet lineage specification.
source: Furthermore, this suggests that maintenance of Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6 expression in the absence of Nkx2.2 is not sufficient for appropriate islet lineage specification.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that despite maintained expression of these factors, Nkx2.2△endo mice still display defective β cell differentiation.

claim: 169 out of 175 significantly regulated genes in Nkx2.2△endo mice were bound by Nkx2.2 within 100 kb of their respective transcriptional start sites.
source: Notably, the majority of the genes regulated by Nkx2.2 appeared to be primary targets: 169/175 of the significantly regulated genes were bound by Nkx2.2 within 100 kb of of their respective transcriptional start sites (TSS) (Figure 3A; Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is supported by cross-referencing RNA-Seq data with ChIP-Seq data.

claim: There was significant overlap (120 genes) of Rfx6 binding near Nkx2.2 target genes.
source: This analysis revealed significant overlap of Rfx6 binding near Nkx2.2 target genes (120 genes, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 4A) and gene ontology (GO) analysis indicated significant representation of genes related to hormone secretion (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by comparative ChIP-Seq analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of genes bound by both Nkx2.2 and Rfx6 indicated significant representation of genes related to hormone secretion.
source: This analysis revealed significant overlap of Rfx6 binding near Nkx2.2 target genes (120 genes, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 4A) and gene ontology (GO) analysis indicated significant representation of genes related to hormone secretion (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was significant overlap (92 genes) between Nkx2.2 target genes and Neurod1 bound genes.
source: Analysis of Neurod1 bound genes revealed similar overlap with Nkx2.2 targets (92 genes, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 4C), and GO analysis identified significant representation of insulin secretion genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by comparative ChIP-Seq analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of genes bound by both Nkx2.2 and Neurod1 identified significant representation of insulin secretion genes.
source: Analysis of Neurod1 bound genes revealed similar overlap with Nkx2.2 targets (92 genes, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 4C), and GO analysis identified significant representation of insulin secretion genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Greater than 75% of the 92 genes simultaneously bound by Nkx2.2 and Neurod1 were also bound by Rfx6.
source: Furthermore, greater than 75% of the 92 genes simultaneously bound by Nkx2.2 and Neurod1 in the same or nearby regulatory regions were also bound by Rfx6 (72 genes, Figure 4E), demonstrating novel regulatory co-operation between these three transcription factors.
evidence: This is supported by comparative ChIP-Seq analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: There is novel regulatory co-operation between Nkx2.2, Neurod1, and Rfx6.
source: Furthermore, greater than 75% of the 92 genes simultaneously bound by Nkx2.2 and Neurod1 in the same or nearby regulatory regions were also bound by Rfx6 (72 genes, Figure 4E), demonstrating novel regulatory co-operation between these three transcription factors.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of significant co-occupancy of these three transcription factors at target genes.

claim: Mlxipl, Mafa, Gast, and G6pc2 expression were decreased at E15.5 in Nkx2.2△endo embryos.
source: (F) RNA-Seq shows decreased Mlxipl, Mafa, Gast, and G6pc2 expression at E15.5 in Nkx2.2△endo embryos. Dotted line refers to 1.0 fold change. (***) p<0.001.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Nkx2.2, Rfx6, and Neurod1 show overlapping binding peaks at the Mlxipl locus.
source: (G) Nkx2.2, Rfx6, and Neurod1 show overlapping binding peaks at Mlxipl locus (mm9 chr5:135,580,783–135,615,792 shown).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data visualization shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Nkx2.2 and Neurod1 show overlapping binding peaks at a region upstream of Mafa.
source: (H) Nkx2.2 and Neurod1 show overlapping binding peaks at a region upstream of Mafa (mm9 chr15:75,577,046–75,587,657 shown).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data visualization shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Nkx2.2 and Rfx6 show overlapping binding peaks upstream of Gast and within intron 1.
source: (I) Nkx2.2 and Rfx6 show overlapping binding peaks upstream of Gast and within intron 1 (mm9 chr11:100,186,915–100,199,407 shown).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data visualization shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Nkx2.2, Rfx6, and Neurod1 show non-overlapping binding peaks near the G6pc2 locus.
source: (J) Non-overlapping Nkx2.2, Rfx6, and Neurod1 binding peaks near G6pc2 locus (mm9 chr2:69,052,146–69,070,781 shown).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data visualization shown in Figure 4J.

claim: The restricted deletion of Nkx2.2 in the Neurog3+ progenitor cells resulted in a phenotype that was remarkably similar to the Nkx2.2KO mice.
source: It was somewhat unexpected that the restricted deletion of Nkx2.2 in the Neurog3+ progenitor cells resulted in a phenotype that was remarkably similar to the Nkx2.2KO mice, which lacked Nkx2.2 throughout pancreas development.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of phenotypic data between Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO mice.

claim: Reduction of Neurog3, Neurod1 and Rfx6 expression is not an obligate step in the mis-specification of islet fates.
source: However, unlike the Nkx2.2KO mice, expression of the essential β cell transcription factors Neurog3, Rfx6, and Neurod1 was unaffected, suggesting that although Nkx2.2 regulates these factors in the pancreatic progenitor population, reduction of Neurog3, Neurod1 and Rfx6 expression is not an obligate step in the mis-specification of islet fates.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that islet mis-specification occurs in Nkx2.2△endo mice despite maintained expression of these factors.

claim: Although Neurog3, Neurod1 and Rfx6 are essential for specifying the β cell program, Nkx2.2 activity must be preserved to facilitate the functional integrity of the β cell regulatory pathway.
source: This may indicate that although Neurog3, Neurod1 and Rfx6 are essential for specifying the β cell program, Nkx2.2 activity must be preserved to facilitate the functional integrity of the β cell regulatory pathway (Figure 5).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that β cell specification fails in Nkx2.2△endo mice despite maintained expression of Neurog3, Neurod1, and Rfx6.

claim: Deletion of Nkx2.2 from the Neurog3+ cells was sufficient to recapitulate the Nkx2.2KO phenotype.
source: Given its early expression in the multipotent progenitor population, it was unexpected that deletion of Nkx2.2 from the Neurog3+ cells was sufficient to recapitulate the Nkx2.2KO phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of phenotypic data between Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO mice.

claim: Neurog3-Cre; Rfx6flox/flox mice display β cell loss similar to the Rfx6null mice.
source: However, it is consistent with a recent study showing that Neurog3-Cre; Rfx6flox/flox mice display β cell loss similar to the Rfx6null mice (Piccand et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: Nkx6.1 functions downstream of Neurog3, with Neurog3-Cre; Nkx6.1flox/flox mice displaying defective β cell differentiation.
source: Similarly, Nkx6.1 functions downstream of Neurog3, with Neurog3-Cre; Nkx6.1flox/floxmice displaying defective β cell differentiation (Schaffer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: The endocrine progenitor cell, downstream of Neurog3 induction, is the primary site of islet cell specification.
source: These studies provide evidence that the endocrine progenitor cell, downstream of Neurog3 induction, is the primary site of islet cell specification.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that conditional deletion of key transcription factors in the Neurog3+ lineage recapitulates null phenotypes.

claim: Unlike mice, NKX2.2 in human islets is only first detected after the appearance of NEUROG3 progenitors.
source: The importance of Nkx2.2 function downstream of Neurog3 expression is also consistent with the timing of NKX2.2 in human islets; unlike mice, NKX2.2 is only first detected after the appearance of NEUROG3 progenitors (Jennings et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: Nkx2.2 function within the mouse Pdx1+ pancreatic progenitor was not sufficient to allow correct islet cell specification and β cell formation.
source: However, while Nkx2.2 function within the mouse Pdx1+ pancreatic progenitor was not sufficient to allow correct islet cell specification and β cell formation, further studies would be required to determine whether Nkx2.2 has additional functions at this earlier stage of pancreas development.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that deletion of Nkx2.2 in the Neurog3+ lineage recapitulates the null phenotype.

claim: The phenotypes of Nkx2.2△endo mice were not as severe as observed in the Nkx2.2KO mice.
source: Although deletion of Nkx2.2 in the endocrine progenitor population appears to grossly phenocopy the Nkx2.2KO phenotype, the phenotypes were not as severe as observed in the Nkx2.2KO mice.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of phenotypic data between Nkx2.2△endo and Nkx2.2KO mice.

claim: There were over 300 genes significantly altered in Nkx2.2KO pancreas that were unchanged in the Nkx2.2△endo mice.
source: In addition, there were over 300 genes significantly altered in Nkx2.2KO pancreas that were unchanged in the Nkx2.2△endo mice (Figure 3A; Table 4).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Deletion of the conserved tinman domain of Nkx2.2 resulted in both aberrant endocrine cell specification and reprogramming of β cells to the α cell fate.
source: Alternatively, deletion of the conserved tinman (TN) domain of Nkx2.2 resulted in both aberrant endocrine cell specification and reprogramming of β cells to the α cell fate (Papizan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: Deletion of Nkx2.2 from β cells after their specification resulted in β cell reprogramming into alternative endocrine lineages and the appearance of islet cells expressing more than one hormone.
source: Furthermore, recent studies in which Nkx2.2 was deleted from β cells after their specification resulted in β cell reprogramming into alternative endocrine lineages and the appearance of islet cells expressing more than one hormone (Gutiérrez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: The phenotype of the Nkx2.2△endo mice most closely resembles the Nkx2.2KO mice, and there is no evidence of reprogramming or multi-hormonal expressing endocrine cells in the mutant islets.
source: Interestingly, the phenotype of the Nkx2.2△endo mice most closely resembles the Nkx2.2KO mice, and we do not see evidence of reprogramming or multi-hormonal expressing (transient or stable) endocrine cells in the mutant islets.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data showing distinct hormone-expressing cell populations.

claim: The best explanation for the discrepant PP phenotype is that the Nkx2.2 null allele was moved to a C57Bl6/J background for this study.
source: Since re-evaluation of Ppy expression in the Nkx2.2KO mice revealed a similar phenotype, the increase in PP is likely not due to a unique function of Nkx2.2 in the pancreatic progenitor to specify PP cells. The best explanation for the discrepant PP phenotype is that we moved the Nkx2.2 null allele to a C57Bl6/J background for this study.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the mechanism underlying the observed phenotype.

claim: A subset of the PP population is derived from Ghrl-expressing ε cells.
source: The upregulation of PP is also interesting since it parallels the increase we observed with ε cells. Consistent with the observation that a subset of the PP population is derived from Ghrl-expressing ε cells (Arnes et al., 2012a), PP+Ghrl+ cells can be infrequently found in Nkx2.2△endo mice at P0 (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous research study.

claim: PP+Ghrl+ cells can be infrequently found in Nkx2.2△endo mice at P0.
source: The upregulation of PP is also interesting since it parallels the increase we observed with ε cells. Consistent with the observation that a subset of the PP population is derived from Ghrl-expressing ε cells (Arnes et al., 2012a), PP+Ghrl+ cells can be infrequently found in Nkx2.2△endo mice at P0 (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: There is an upregulation of Arx expression in Nkx2.2△endo mice, which has previously been shown to induce enhanced PP cell formation.
source: Furthermore, we observe an upregulation of Arx expression, which has also previously been shown to induce enhanced PP cell formation (Collombat et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by data from the study and citation to a previous research study.

claim: This study identifies a novel critical window for Nkx2.2-mediated regulation of islet cell specification within the Neurog3 lineage following induction of Neurog3.
source: Our results identify a novel critical window for Nkx2.2-mediated regulation of islet cell specification within the Neurog3 lineage following induction of Neurog3.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that deletion of Nkx2.2 specifically in the Neurog3+ lineage recapitulates the null phenotype.

claim: Although Nkx2.2 appears to function near the top of the islet transcriptional hierarchy, maintained Nkx2.2 activity is also a necessary component of the regulatory networks functioning downstream of Neurog3 to induce β cell specification.
source: Furthermore, although Nkx2.2 appears to function near the top of the islet transcriptional hierarchy, we demonstrate that maintained Nkx2.2 activity is also a necessary component of the regulatory networks functioning downstream of Neurog3 to induce β cell specification.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that β cell specification fails in Nkx2.2△endo mice despite maintained expression of downstream factors.

claim: Different combinations of Nkx2.2, Rfx6, and Neurod1 directly regulate important genes in the β cell pathways.
source: Our discovery that different combinations of the set of transcription factors analyzed in this study directly regulate important genes in the β cell pathways raises important questions about the complex nature of cell-specific gene regulation that may have important implications for β cell induction, maturation and function.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq co-occupancy analysis showing various patterns of binding at target genes.
